title: Red Queen Effect
equation: Competitive Position = Internal Improvement Rate ÷ Market Improvement Rate
hook: You're working harder than ever and still losing ground. That's because your competitors are working harder too.
statement: In a market where everyone keeps improving, you have to keep getting faster just to stay in place.
explainer: Busy doesn't mean ahead. The floor keeps rising whether you move or not. Companies that stopped keeping pace got left behind, while the ones that kept speeding up pulled away.
sop: Compare your improvement rate to the market average.
Find where you're falling below the curve.
Speed up improvements in your core product.
Add a few bold bets to get ahead somewhere new.
equation_example: You ship 3 meaningful improvements a quarter. Competitors ship 4. Internal Improvement Rate 3 ÷ Market Improvement Rate 4 = 0.75, so 75% of market pace. Above 100% means you're pulling ahead. Below means the floor is outrunning you.
question: Count the real improvements you shipped last quarter, then count what your top competitor shipped.
closing_statement: Standing still is falling behind in a moving market.
caption:
Principle Nº 319: Red Queen Effect

You're working harder than ever and still losing ground. That's because your competitors are working harder too.

In a market where everyone keeps improving, you have to keep getting faster just to stay in place.

Your turn: Count the real improvements you shipped last quarter, then count what your top competitor shipped.
